minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission voted to seek Opera funds for old-stone repair and back-field site planning, and approved smaller spends.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the superintendent's update on mowing, hiring and burials, then voted on solar lights, a partial lot refund, hedge trimming, software licence and a skirt repair. Much of the meeting covered perpetual care and lot-sale funds, the need for more maintenance money, and which projects to send to the select board for Opera funds. A resident raised questions about lot capacity and perpetual care at the end.

public_comment.topic: Reported North Cemetery looks much better, with a worker using a weed whacker, and thanked those responsible.
Recommended public comment at the start and end of meetings; asked about annual lot sales, perpetual care, lot prices and capacity, and urged incremental planning and careful spending.

budget_items.what_was_said: Balances and yearly interest were reviewed, and the commission wants to know the investment return percentage before the Finance Committee meeting.
Contract mowing help was discussed as an addition to the purchase of service line, or a full-time hire.
Lake View quote was accepted, paid from the commission's budget.
Annual licence and maintenance support fees approved.
Cleaning of the Allen stone was paid from a trust, not the budget.
A letter to the select board will request a share of uncommitted funds; earlier earmark request mentioned.
Spending approved up to a cap to avoid a second vote.
Old stone restoration and back field site planning chosen as the two projects.
Perpetual care and lot price stated in answer to a resident.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to send two projects to the select board for Opera funds: old stone repair and cleaning, and back field site planning; the vote was not audible.
The commission accepted the solar lighting payment for North and South Cemetery, the Lake View shrub-trimming quote, and the Rain Maker software licence, each passing.
The commission approved South Cemetery skirt repair up to a stated cap, so a second vote would not be needed.
A refund to the family for four returned burial lots was voted, but the outcome is not audible. Refund policy and form review was put off to the next meeting.
Maintenance funding was tabled, and the superintendent will bring a firm count of open lots and niche wall spaces next meeting.

why_it_matters: Opera funds are a one-time source the select board controls, so the commission's request for old-stone repair and back-field planning competes with other town needs rather than coming out of its own budget.

The commission also left open how to pay for more mowing, either contract help or a hire, and the lot count it will bring back bears on how long the cemeteries can keep selling lots and how much perpetual care money supports them.
watch_next: The superintendent's firm count of open lots and niche wall spaces at the next commission meeting.
The commission's letter to the select board requesting Opera funds, and the select board's response.

Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the solar lights, the Lakeview trimming, the Rain Maker/Ramaker payment and the skirt repair. They differ on the two votes our captions could not hear, where the official minutes give the motions and the 3-0 outcomes. The one thing to check is the maintenance-funding decision: ours says it was tabled, and the official minutes say the DPW Director was directed to check numbers and ask the town for more money.
